rv.q: His naivety verges on the comic, but the play is at its most gripping when it takes the opinions of this specialist in economic history seriously.
A powerful rendering of a moment that still leaves one uneasy; what happened next in real life minutes after this meeting is still disputed.

cn.t: Jack MacGregor's play earns praise for dramatizing a compelling true incident—a Scottish academic's 1978 encounter with Pol Pot—exploring power dynamics and moral complexity with effective storytelling.
